Losing someone you are close to really sucks. There is no way around it. But... their life is over. Yours continues. Live what little time you have. You have very little time. This isn't a depressing truth; this is simply the truth. It is inescapable. So, enjoy everything. Would you want loved ones to burn themselves up pining for you after you pass? Or would you want them to enjoy what little time they have? I'm not saying grief is wrong. Grief is necessary.

However, keep in mind that every second that ticks past is irretrievable, irrevocable, and nonexchangeable. Time is the greatest opportunity cost we have. Very few people talk about this because it's easier to talk about the opportunity cost of money. Money comes and goes. Time does not. You have a finite amount and you will not acquire more. You cannot declare bankruptcy and start over. So, I'll say it again - find a way to enjoy everything.

Live. Live to your fullest. Experience everything that you feel like you need to - that your friend would have liked. Dedicate the love you have for him to others around you and spread the love - the care - around you as much as possible, since the little bit of extra effort you take to do it will not only honor the memory of the one you've lost, but also benefit others around you. Visit your local pet shelter, or buy a homeless guy some takeout or volunteer at your church or soup kitchen - do it for the soul that has left this world to find peace, if not for you to find it yourself. In their name.
